fonts: Century Gothic.ttf, Century Gothic Bold.ttf, Century Gothic Italic.ttf, Century Gothic Bold Italic.ttf (Word DFonts)
source.probe: advance-matched Liberation Sans derivative (tools/build-metric-fonts.py): hmtx = Century Gothic DFonts advances exactly; Word paces Century Gothic at its hmtx (production PDF char origins / hmtx = 1.000 for lowercase and digits, 0.99 for kerned capitals)

note:
Century Gothic ships only inside Office (Word's DFonts), so Chromium fell to
the Helvetica-class sans: ~9% narrower per body line (hmtx of both fonts,
2026-09-12). Its geometry is not a uniform scale of Liberation Sans (per glyph
0.81-1.43: s 1.29, a 0.81, T 1.43), so 2026-09-12 fitted one size-adjusted face per
case class; the widths matched on average but drifted both ways over long
documents and size-adjust scaled the glyph height with the width, so capitals and
digits sat visibly smaller than the lowercase in one line (13.3/11.4/12.0 pt pieces of
a 12 pt line). The ranged faces are now one advance-matched derivative per cut
(CenturyGothicGO-*.ttf, tools/build-metric-fonts.py): Liberation Sans outlines
scaled horizontally to each Word advance, one vertical factor, Word advances in
hmtx. Production PDFs pace Century Gothic at its hmtx exactly (lowercase and
digits 1.000; capitals 0.96-0.99 only where w:kern is on, not baked in). The
rangeless Liberation Sans face keeps the non-Latin fallback. Pitch stays the probed
1.226 (`lineHeightFactor`).
